exposure: medical indications for CS (threatened miscarriage, anemia, preeclampsia, gestational hypertension, gestational diabetes mellitus)
cohort: The study included a convenient sample of 345 female physicians and medical students who had delivered by Cesarean Section in Babylon Governorate.
finding: The cesarean section rate among female physicians and medical students in Babylon Governorate was significantly higher than the WHO recommended optimal range, with patient's wishes due to fear of vaginal delivery pain being the primary indication for CS.
mod_finding: A significant proportion (43.2%) of CSs were due to patient's wishes, with 77.2% of those having CS without medical reason, primarily due to fear of vaginal delivery pain.
cross-section timing: Data was collected over a period of 5 months.
gest_age: 89.6% of deliveries occurred after 37 weeks of gestation.
